spec: Build a REST API for personal notes. Users can create, list, fetch, update and delete notes. Each note has a title, body and timestamps. Notes are stored in DynamoDB.

plan.summary: A REST API for managing personal notes, allowing users to create, list, fetch, update, and delete notes. Each note has a title, body, and creation/update timestamps. Notes are persisted in DynamoDB.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new note with a title and body.
Fetch a single note by its ID.
Update an existing note's title and/or body.
Delete a note by its ID.

aws_resources.name: notes
aws_resources.justification: Primary storage for note records as explicitly required by the spec; note_id serves as the partition key.

aws_resources.name: personal-notes-api-gateway
aws_resources.justification: Exposes the REST API endpoints for creating, listing, fetching, updating, and deleting notes.

aws_resources.name: personal-notes-handler
aws_resources.justification: Runs the FastAPI application to process API requests against DynamoDB.

aws_resources.name: personal-notes-lambda-role
aws_resources.justification: Grants the Lambda function permission to read/write the DynamoDB table and write logs to CloudWatch.

aws_resources.name: personal-notes-logs
aws_resources.justification: Captures Lambda execution logs for observability and debugging.

assumptions: No authentication or user identity is specified; the API treats all notes as a single shared personal namespace without per-user partitioning.
note_id is a server-generated UUID used as the DynamoDB partition key.
Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are generated server-side in ISO 8601 UTC format.
The API returns and accepts JSON payloads.
Listing notes performs a full table scan since no pagination or filtering was specified.
The FastAPI app is deployed as a Lambda behind API Gateway using an ASGI adapter (e.g., Mangum).

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 5 files — FastAPI personal notes API with a DynamoDB storage layer behind a NoteRepository interface. app.py defines the CRUD endpoints and dependency-injected repository; storage.py provides DynamoDBNoteRepository (LocalStack-aware via AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, table from NOTES_TABLE) and an InMemoryNoteRepository used by tests. Tests inject the in-memory repo so they run fully offline. Includes requirements.txt and README.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for personal_notes_api on LocalStack-compatible services. Includes a DynamoDB table (note_id hash key) with SSE and point-in-time recovery; a Python Lambda packaged inline via local_file + archive_file (no pre-built artifact) with tracing, reserved concurrency, and environment table binding; a least-privilege IAM role scoped to the specific table ARN, its log group, and X-Ray; two CloudWatch log groups (Lambda + API access) with 365-day retention; and an API Gateway REST API with proxy+root AWS_PROXY integrations, access logging, X-Ray tracing, method settings, deployment, stage, and Lambda invoke permission. Provider pins hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 with default project/managed-by tags. Every resource maps to the plan's aws_resources list.
